10.15.4
Secondary-Output Load and Thermal Tests
The electronic load was connected to the V2 secondary output. At approximately 240 V
AC and 50 Hz, increasing the load current from 1.86 A to 10.01 A raised the calculated
secondary power from 48.68 W to 137.08 W. The secondary voltage fell from 26.14 V to
13.69 V over this sequence (table 10.13 and fig. 10.14). At 20.07 V, the load drew 4.29 A,
giving 86.17 W. The higher-power points were therefore reached with increasing voltage
droop.

In the thermal images in fig. 10.15, the input-bridge region R3 reached 83.9 ◦C near
70.75 W. Its maxima at the subsequent higher-power points were lower, between 68.2 ◦C
and 75.6 ◦C. The secondary region R1 became progressively hotter, rising from 50.3 ◦C
to 98.3 ◦C.
None of the load points reached thermal equilibrium. The sequence includes both load
changes and continued heating, so the temperatures cannot be treated as settled values
for each power level. Diode selection and the current and thermal paths around the rec-
tifiers require further work. The tests show that the leakage-only stage can transfer more
than 100 W to a secondary load, although voltage droop and continued heating remain.
